# ontologyDiscoverR

**AI-assisted ontology discovery from documents and schemas.**

`ontologyDiscoverR` uses a large language model — any provider supported by
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) — to extract ontology structure (object
types, properties, link types, action types and concept definitions) from
database schemas, API specs, documentation and data files. The output is a
canonical [ontologySpecR](https://github.com/CathalByrneGit/ontologySpecR)
bundle, built with the spec constructors and checked with
`ontologySpecR::validate_bundle()`, ready for the rest of the ecosystem.

## Installation

```{r install}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("cathalbyrnegit/ontologydiscoverr")
```

Choose an LLM provider (there is no built-in default; see
[LLM providers](#llm-providers)):

```{r provider}
options(ontologyDiscoverR.chat = "openai/gpt-4.1")   # or pass llm = to discover_session()
```

## How it works

The package has two phases, each powered by the LLM provider you choose
(Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama or any other ellmer backend):

```
Phase 1 — Schema discovery
  Source documents / schemas / APIs
            ↓  parse → extract → merge → review
       ontologySpecR bundle (validated)

Phase 2 — Population
       ontology bundle  +  document corpus
            ↓  extract instances → validate against schema
       named data frames  +  edge list  +  provenance table
```

**Phase 1** runs three sequential LLM passes per source:

1. **Object types** — entities with identity (tables, schema components, named domain concepts)
2. **Link types** — relationships between object types (FK constraints, API references, document links)
3. **Action types & concept hints** — verbs/endpoints and business-rule conditions

**Phase 2** takes the bundle from phase 1 and extracts *specific named instances* from a
document corpus. Instances are validated against the schema; unrecognised properties are
flagged as schema amendment candidates.

## Quick start

### Phase 1 — Schema discovery

```{r phase1}
library(ontologyDiscoverR)

sess <- discover_session("hospital-demo", llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1"))

# Or use a local model for sensitive data:
# sess <- discover_session("investigation", llm = ellmer::chat_ollama(model = "llama3.3"))

sess   <- dis_add_file(sess, "path/to/hospital-schema.sql")
sess   <- dis_extract(sess, verbose = TRUE)
sess   <- dis_review(sess)   # optional Shiny review app
bundle <- dis_to_bundle(sess, bundle_id = "hospital-v1", bundle_name = "Hospital Ontology")
ontologySpecR::write_bundle(bundle, "hospital-v1.json")
```

### Phase 2 — Population

```{r phase2}
pop <- populate_session(schema = bundle)
pop <- pop_add_corpus(pop, "path/to/documents/")
pop <- pop_extract(pop, verbose = TRUE)

records <- pop_to_records(pop)
records$instances$Person   # data frame: instance_id, name, role, ...
records$relationships       # from_instance_id, to_instance_id, link_type_id, evidence
records$provenance          # instance_id, source_label, excerpt, confidence

edges <- pop_to_edgelist(pop)   # from, to, type, weight, evidence — ready for graph packages
pop_amendments(pop)             # schema properties flagged during extraction
pop_save(pop, "session.rds")    # save/resume for large corpora
```

## Supported source types

| Source type | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SQL DDL file | `parse_sql_ddl()` | CREATE TABLE → object types, FK → link types |
| Live database | `parse_db_schema()` | DBI connection, reads information_schema |
| OpenAPI spec | `parse_openapi()` | 3.x + Swagger 2.x, YAML or JSON |
| CSV file | `parse_csv()` | Header + sample rows, type inference |
| R data frame | `parse_r_dataframe()` | In-memory, includes `str()` for LLM context |
| PDF | `parse_pdf()` | Text extracted via `pdftools`, up to 50k chars |
| Markdown / HTML | `parse_markdown()` / `parse_html()` | Heading structure preserved |
| OWL / RDF | `parse_owl()` | Classes → object types, properties → links |

## LLM providers

`llm` accepts an ellmer Chat object, a `"provider/model"` string (passed to
`ellmer::chat()`), or a `function(system_prompt)` returning a Chat. With
`llm = NULL`, `getOption("ontologyDiscoverR.chat")` and then the
`ONTOLOGYDISCOVERR_CHAT` environment variable are used; if neither is set,
discovery stops with an error explaining how to choose one.

```{r providers}
discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_anthropic())
discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1"))
discover_session("demo", llm = ellmer::chat_google_gemini())
discover_session("demo", llm = "ollama/llama3.3")   # local: nothing leaves your machine
```

Structured output is used when the provider supports it. The provider and model
are recorded in `sess$llm_info` and on every candidate (`extracted_by`). See
"Choosing a model" in `vignette("from-schema")` for tips on small local models.

## Live database example

```{r db}
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)

con  <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "hospital.ddb")
sess <- discover_session("from-db")
sess <- dis_add_db(sess, con, label = "hospital-db")
sess <- dis_extract(sess)
```

## Confidence scores

Every extracted candidate carries a confidence score (0–1):

| Score | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1.0 | Explicitly defined in schema / data dictionary |
| 0.9 | Clearly named in documentation with attributes listed |
| 0.7 | Mentioned as a concept with some structure implied |
| 0.5 | Inferred from context |
| 0.2 | Speculative |

Use `min_confidence` in `dis_to_bundle()` to control which pending candidates
are included:

```{r confidence}
bundle <- dis_to_bundle(sess, "my-bundle", "My Ontology", min_confidence = 0.7)
```

## Interactive review

```{r review}
sess <- dis_review(sess)
```

The Shiny app has four panels:

- **Object Types** — approve/reject individual candidates or bulk-approve all ≥ 0.8 confidence
- **Link Types** — correct from/to endpoints if the LLM misidentified them
- **Concept Hints** — edit the suggested SQL expression inline, test against a live DB
- **Conflicts** — resolve pairs of conflicting candidates side by side

## MCP conversational building

With [ontologyAPI](https://github.com/CathalByrneGit/ontologyAPI) installed,
you can build the ontology interactively over MCP:

```{r mcp}
server <- ontologyAPI::mcp_server(ontologyAPI::ontology_service(existing_bundle, con))
dis_add_mcp_tool(server, sess)     # registers "build_ontology"
ontologyAPI::serve_mcp(server)

# Now an LLM agent can say things like:
# "Add a link from Hospital to Patient called Admission"
# "The Patient object type should have a concept called high_risk where age > 65"
# "Looks good — generate the bundle"
```

## Testing

The test suite runs on a fake ellmer Chat: no network, no API key, no cost.
Optional live smoke tests run per provider when its credentials are present and
`ONTOLOGYDISCOVERR_LIVE_TESTS=true`.

```{r test}
devtools::test()
```

## Package structure

```
R/
  session.R           # discover_session, dis_add_*, dis_extract, dis_summary
  bundle.R            # dis_to_bundle(): candidates -> ontologySpecR bundle
  llm.R               # call_llm(), provider resolution, structured output
  llm_types.R         # ellmer type specs for every structured call
  parse_*.R           # one file per source type
  extract.R           # four LLM extraction passes
  merge.R             # merge_candidates, detect_conflicts
  candidates.R        # S3 constructors for all four candidate types
  review.R            # dis_review() Shiny app
  mcp_builder.R       # dis_add_mcp_tool(), pop_add_mcp_tool() (needs ontologyAPI)
  types.R             # normalise_type, validate_candidate
  utils.R             # UUID, truncation, JSON helpers

inst/fixtures/        # example-schema.sql, example-openapi.yaml,
                      # example-docs.md, example-data.csv

tests/testthat/       # mocked-LLM tests for all modules
vignettes/            # four how-to vignettes
```
